newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong blue chips end weak, red chips bouyant.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong blue chips end weak, red chips bouyant.

text.p: Hong Kong blue chips ended weak on Monday as concerns that interest rates may move higher over coming weeks prompted investors to shun interest rate sensitive stocks and turn to China-related issues.
The Hang Seng Index closed on a loss of 68.59 points, or 0.51 percent, at 13,268.76. Turnover was a heavy HK$13.11 billion compared with HK$10.84 billion on Friday.
"There is a lot of speculative money betting on the red chips while banking and property are still a little bit quiet," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
"People think interest rates will pick up sooner or later."
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting meeting is scheduled for March 25. Analysts said they could not rule out a hike in interest rates following recent economic data.
"Our view is still that there will not be a rate hike but the probability of a rate hike has increased," said Abhijit Chakrabortti, senior strategist at Lehman Brothers.
Although U.S. February employment data showed tame wage growth, 339,000 new non-farm jobs were created last month, outstripping forecasts of an average 230,000 new jobs.

"The market has been dominated by other issues -- political issues, valuation issues, overownership issues, earnings issues recently -- but I think that what this employment number has done is start to focus concentration back on the rate issue," said Chakrabortti.
"I think in that sense the market will remain on tenterhooks," he added.

Meanwhile China-related red chips moved ahead. "I think quite a few have already announced asset injections. Quite a number of them are still under negotation with the parent company so people expect more from them," said one analyst.
Shares in Continental Mariner Investment Co Ltd rose HK$0.35 to HK$4.55. The company said it was planning to buy China properties from its parent.

Shares in Shum Yip Investment Ltd gained HK$0.775 to HK$5.30. The company, which is backed by the Shenzhen municipal government, made its stock market debut on Friday. "A lot of this speculative money is pumping the stock," said Ng.
Among the blue chips, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd fell HK$1.00 to HK$57.50, Swire Pacific Ltd dropped HK$0.75 to HK$65.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd shed HK$1.25 to HK$87.50.
